absent: Construction and contents of format permission and protection-key mask tables.
Passthrough bit refresh policy and shadow access mask values.
TDP level selection and maximum huge-page level policy.
NX huge-page recovery timing, ratio semantics and mitigation disable conditions.
Reverse-map lock implementation and single versus many synchronization.
Shadow walk initialization, validity and stepping internals.
Shadow entry set, clear, update and present-test primitives.
Memslot generation advancement and invalidation sequencing.
Remote TLB flush range selection and ordering guarantees.
Reclaim path that removes pages from possible NX huge-page lists.

findings.text: MMIO shadow entry builder is shared with other MMU code and combines current memslot generation with host reserved markers, filtered access rights and guest address into a nonpresent entry.
NX huge page candidate tracker is shared with other MMU code and records a shadow page once for later reclaim while updating global split and per-type pending counters.
TDP dirty write-protect helper for a masked page range is shared with other MMU code and applies the operation across every valid root in the slot address space.
Global mode controls for two-dimensional paging, TDP MMU enablement, eager large-page splitting, NX huge-page policy and the shadow page header cache are shared across the MMU.

Fault decision consults refreshed passthrough state and a format permission table indexed by fault error bits with supervisor override folded in, then adds protection-key denial derived from current key rights, domain index and user versus supervisor access, returning either no fault or present plus optional key error.
An address counts as direct when the VM configures no direct bits or when the address carries at least one configured direct bit.

MMIO shadow entries round-trip guest frame, access subset and generation; validation fails during concurrent memslot updates and otherwise requires stored generation to equal current memslot generation.

Guest access for a shadow page comes from per-index shadowed translation when present, otherwise from the page role for direct or passthrough pages; stored translation updates validate consistency for the latter.
Large-page use for a frame is denied when disallowed in its slot at that level, including the peer address space when two address spaces exist.
Reverse-map head distinguishes empty, single pointer and descriptor-list encodings, with chained descriptors keeping tails full and growing from the head on overflow.
Candidate tracking is idempotent per page via list membership and accounts splits globally plus pending pages per MMU type.
Dirty-bitmap slot resolution rejects missing or invalid slots and optionally rejects slots with dirty tracking enabled.
Dirty clearing selects the writable bit when write protection is required and the dirty bit otherwise, skipping entries already clear and only touching small leaves covered by the mask.
TDP MMU lockless path is active only when both the global TDP MMU switch and the current root direct role are set.
Lockless shadow walks always pair begin with end using the same MMU-type branch so TDP and legacy protection cannot mix.
NX huge-page tunables expose a tri-state master switch plus recovery period and ratio controls with custom get and set operations.
Read-only reverse-map acquisition disables preemption only while a non-empty snapshot is held and restores it on release.
Masked TDP dirty clearing runs under write-held MMU lock with an inner RCU read section covering the leaf iteration.

Legacy lockless walks block teardown by disabling interrupts and publishing a reading state with ordered stores, then restoring outside-guest state with release semantics before re-enabling interrupts.
TDP lockless walks enter and exit an RCU read section without changing interrupt or vcpu mode state.
Shared TDP entries that may be observed without exclusive lock use an atomic bit-clear primitive, while private entries use a plain write.
Reverse-map list node holds a next link, counts for local and tail entries, and a fixed array of shadow entry pointers sized by the list extension constant.
Shadow walk position holds guest address, shadow address, current pointer, level and index.
MMU role register snapshot carries control register zero, control register four and extended feature register values.
Reverse-map iterator holds an opaque head reference plus current descriptor and position used to yield successive shadow pointers.
Split shadow entry view overlays a 64-bit entry with low and high 32-bit halves to allow ordered narrow reads.
Reverse-map storage moves from empty to single pointer to small list to chained list as entries are added, and full zap collapses any state back to empty after freeing chain nodes.
An MMIO entry is created with the current generation, stays valid while generations match, and becomes invalid on memslot generation change or during an update window.
Shadow traversal initializes position from root and address, tests validity, advances stepwise, and the lockless form additionally snapshots each entry before presenting it.
Single-entry zap clears tracking bits and unlinks one pointer while preserving remaining list state; full zap clears every pointer and resets the head.
Fault permission evaluator serves as the access-check entry combining privilege, supervisor override, format permissions and protection keys.
Guest control register reader and remote TLB availability plus per-entry flush helpers serve as MMU coordination entries.
Lockless shadow entry reader is the safe dereference entry for concurrent walks, delegating to a platform-specific snapshot primitive.
Reverse-map list add and iterator advance plus traversal macros are the mutation and visit entries for reverse maps.
Masked dirty write-protect across TDP and legacy reverse maps is the dirty-tracking coordination entry.
On platforms without atomic wide loads, lockless reads retry when the low half changes or a concurrent clear counter advances, preventing torn snapshots.
Unexpected protection-key, single-step or reserved bits in the incoming fault code trigger a one-time warning because callers are expected to strip nested paging codes.
Access or frame mismatches when recording translation under direct or passthrough pages trigger one-time warnings since role-derived values must already agree.
Treating an MMIO entry as valid while a memslot update is in progress would be unsafe, so validation unconditionally fails in that window.
Lockless reverse-map traversal may observe cleared entries, so only entries still present after the lockless snapshot are visited.
Entries needing write protection must clear writability rather than only the dirty bit; mixing the paths would lose tracking.
Reverse-map descriptor capacity is fourteen entries.
Shadow prefetch window covers eight entries.
Reverse-map multi-entry marker occupies bit zero.
Reverse-map locked marker occupies bit one.
Mixed large-page marker occupies bit thirty-one.
